images.alt: A Compaq AlphaServer ES40 tower next to another DEC server and a monitor
images.caption: A Compaq AlphaServer ES40 — the exact class of machine emulated here, DEC's own iron built around its own 64-bit Alpha processor.

images.alt: A close-up view of an AlphaServer ES40 chassis with its front panel and drive bays visible
images.caption: The ES40's front bays, built for the workload Tru64 5.1B was engineered against: DEC hardware running the operating system DEC wrote for it.

images.alt: A DEC AlphaServer 2100A pedestal-chassis server tower, photographed from the front
images.caption: A DEC AlphaServer 2100A pedestal server — an earlier member of the same AlphaServer line Tru64 was tested against release after release.

images.alt: The interior of a decommissioned DEC AlphaServer 1000A, showing the CPU board and heat sink mounting
images.caption: Inside an AlphaServer: the CPU board and its heat sink, the kind of Alpha silicon Tru64's AdvFS and TruCluster were built to drive.

images.alt: The interior of a DEC AlphaServer 2100 with its case open, showing internal boards and cabling
images.caption: The inside of an AlphaServer 2100 — server-class Alpha hardware from the same family line as the ES40 emulated here.
